title: Scheme tests of the relative diagonal of an algebraic-space morphism
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $g:U\to V$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Form $W=U\times_VU$ and its diagonal $\Delta_g:U\to W$, using sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For every $B$-scheme $T$ and morphism $T\to W$, the sheaf fibre product $D_T=U\times_WT$ is represented by a scheme, and its projection $d_T:D_T\to T$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and a monomorphism. Here a monomorphism means that for every scheme $Z$ and maps $a,b:Z\to D_T$, $d_Ta=d_Tb$ implies $a=b$. No finiteness assumption on $g$, $U$, $V$ or $B$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03HK (lemma-properties-diagonal), (1)--(3); scheme tests are spaces.tex Tag 025V (definition-relative-representable-property).

proof.text: Write $t=(t_1,t_2):T\to U\times_VU$, so $gt_1=gt_2$. By [def-trf-algebraic-space], the diagonal of $U$ over $B$ is representable. Its pullback along $(t_1,t_2):T\to U\times_BU$ is therefore a scheme $E$. For every $B$-scheme $Z$, both $E(Z)$ and $D_T(Z)$ consist of maps $z:Z\to T$ with $t_1z=t_2z$: in the latter fibre product the other coordinate is forced to equal $t_1z$. These identifications commute with restriction, so they identify the two sheaves and represent $D_T$ by $E$. Here the sheaf products and their universal properties are [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 03HK (lemma-properties-diagonal), first proof paragraph: representability; equality-locus argument expanded using spaces.tex Tag 025Y

proof.text: The same description proves monomorphy. A map $Z\to D_T$ is uniquely determined by its projection $z:Z\to T$, because its $U$-coordinate must be $t_1z$. Hence two maps with equal projections coincide. For a scheme $Z$ without a specified $B$-structure, the common projection supplies the structure $Z\to T\to B$, making both maps $B$-morphisms. Thus the assertion holds for every scheme $Z$, as required by the statement. This uses only the representability and natural-transformation conventions of [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 03HK (lemma-properties-diagonal), assertion (3): pointwise proof of the diagonal and its base changes being monomorphisms

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $a:A\to U$ from a scheme using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Put $R=A\times_UA$ and $P=A\times_VA$. Both are schemes: they are the pullbacks of the representable diagonals of $U$ and $V$ along $A\times_BA$; scheme products exist by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The first projection $s:R\to A$ is etale, being a scheme test of $a$. The map $q:P\to W$ factors as $A\times_VA\to A\times_VU\to U\times_VU$, each arrow a base change of $a$, on the second and first coordinate respectively. Thus $q$ is representable surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. There is a map $r:R\to P$ induced by $g$. The square with top $r$, bottom $\Delta_g$, and vertical arrows $R\to U$, $q:P\to W$ is cartesian: a pair $(a_1,a_2)$ in $P$ lies over $(u,u)$ exactly when $a(a_1)=a(a_2)=u$, which is precisely an element of $R$.

source.place: Tag 03HK (lemma-properties-diagonal), presentation diagram and its cartesian left square; spaces.tex Tag 025Y; spaces-topologies.tex Tag 041F

proof.text: Since $s:R\to A$ is etale, it is unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence locally of finite type by [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Let $p_1:P\to A$ be the first projection. The composite $p_1r=s$ is locally of finite type, so clause (a) of [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target] gives that $r:R\to P$ is locally of finite type. Only that clause is used: it imposes no hypothesis on $p_1$, in particular no separatedness or quasi-compactness.

For the original test $T\to W$, put $Q=T\times_WP$. Since $q$ is representable surjective etale, $Q$ is a scheme and $Q\to T$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Put $D_Q=D_T\times_TQ$. This is a scheme by [def-pc-fibre-product], and $D_Q\to D_T$ is surjective etale by the same base-change result. The cartesian square in step 3 gives $D_Q\cong R\times_PQ$ over $Q$: on every test scheme either side is a triple $(u,(a_1,a_2),t)$ with $a(a_1)=a(a_2)=u$ and $q(a_1,a_2)=t|_W$. Forgetting or restoring the forced coordinate $u$ gives the inverse natural maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change] to $r:R\to P$ and the scheme morphism $Q\to P$. Thus $D_Q\to Q$ is locally of finite type.

source.place: Tag 02WZ (lemma-representable-morphisms-spaces-property), direct proof with the atlas and arbitrary scheme test; morphisms.tex Tag 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] with the property locally of finite type to the commutative square $D_Q\to Q$ over $D_T\to T$. Both vertical arrows are etale and $D_Q\to D_T$ is surjective, as established in step 5. The top arrow is locally of finite type, so the cited source-and-target criterion gives the same property for $d_T:D_T\to T$. Together with steps 1 and 2 this proves every clause for every test $T\to W$. No step assumed finite type or separation of $g$, $U$, $V$, or $B$.
